messages:
Anya: Quick sync — I'm drafting the Dedicated Capacity PRD (SLA + throughput sizing + autoscale acceptance). Need concrete numbers we can put in the doc today so Eng/Infra can scope. High level asks from sales: stable p99 targets, a clear throughput floor per reservation, and autoscale behavior for bursts.

Rob: Agree. Proposal: define two complementary metrics — a sizing metric (tokens/sec or inference requests/sec per reservation) and an SLO (latency at common seq lengths). Avoid only token-based SLOs because customers vary.

Sasha: From infra: we need mapping to instance families. Rough samples below (very rough perf averages, includes perf with 16k context optimizations):
```
- A100-40: ~9k tokens/s per reserved unit
- H100-80: ~16k tokens/s per reserved unit
- L4/Hopper-ish: ~5-7k tokens/s per reserved unit
```
We should call out assumptions: batch sizes, quantization, KV cache hit >= 60%.

Mike: For SLOs + SLA I'd suggest:
- SLA availability: 99.95% per calendar month (exclusions: planned maintenance windows)
- SLO latency guarantees for GA: p50/p95/p99 at fixed seq lengths. e.g. p99 < 250ms @ 128 tokens, p99 < 450ms @ 512 tokens (measured end-to-end on reserved capacity, steady-state).
- Error budget and rollback policy: if p99 misses for 3 consecutive daily windows, auto-fallback to canary routing and notify customers.

Cecilia: Customers also want short bursts covered. Add acceptance: reserved pools must support 2x provisioned throughput for at least 5 minutes without overall p99 degradation, and 4x sustained burst fallback to hosted with graceful degradation messaging. Sales will want this in PRD for top-tier customers.

Rob: Autoscale rules I want in the PRD draft:
- Scale-up threshold: sustained avg GPU util > 70% for 60s triggers warm-up allocation; target ready-to-serve within 90s.
- Warm pool: keep N warm GPUs (configurable, default 1 per 8 reserved units) to reduce cold-starts.
- Scale-down: idle for 5m -> shrink.
- Autoscale acceptance test: replay 30-minute synthetic trace (with 95th percentile burst windows) and require >=95% requests meet p99 SLA.

Sasha: Cost note: warm pools add ~5-10% committed spend depending on instance family. We'll include a togglable warm-pool flag in PRD and recommended defaults. Also include instance mapping table and a conversion script for customers to translate reserved units -> instance footprint.

Mike: Edge cases / tests to include in PRD: KV cache cold-start, multi-tenant noisy neighbor, long-context degrade mode (trim to safeguard latency). Acceptance criteria: run 10 synthetic traces across seq-length distributions. At least 9/10 traces must meet p99 SLA; no single trace can drop below 90% success.

Anya: Nice. I'll add the numbers and tests to the PRD. Action items:
- Rob: add exact reserved-unit -> instance mapping + conversion script stub (due EOD).
- Sasha: write autoscale warm-pool cost appendix + implementation constraints (tomorrow AM).
- Mike: create SLO test harness + synthetic trace definitions (this week).
- Cecilia: collect top 3 pilot customers and confirm burst expectations (this week).

deploy-bot: New PRD draft uploaded: /prd/dedicated-capacity/sla-throughput-autoscale/draft-v1.md : Anya assigned.

Anya: I'll ping each of you with the PRD link after I push. If anyone wants stricter numbers, drop them here and I'll call out optional tiers (standard, premium) in the doc. :thumbsup:
